scams.name: The Adventure Photo Upsell
scams.tldr: The flight is breathtaking and your pilot takes photos and video the entire time.
scams.description: The flight is breathtaking and your pilot takes photos and video the entire time. But back on the ground, you're told the photo and video package is an additional 60 to 100 CHF, and without it, you get nothing. Your pilot has already uploaded the best shots to their device, and there's no option to use your own camera during the flight. Swiss travel forums and TripAdvisor reviews note that some Interlaken adventure operators deliberately keep photo pricing vague during booking so the post-flight upsell catches you when you're still buzzing with adrenaline.
scams.avoidance: Ask specifically about photo and video package costs before booking any adventure activity. Some operators include media in the price -- compare total costs including photos across companies. Ask in advance whether you can bring and mount your own GoPro or action camera. Book through established operators like Paragliding Interlaken or Skywings that clearly list all fees. Budget an extra 40-80 CHF for media when planning adventure activities in Interlaken.
scams.location: Paragliding and skydiving operators along Hohematte park and Hauptstrasse

scams.name: The Souvenir Shop Tourist Tax
scams.tldr: The prices aren't displayed on the items.
scams.description: The prices aren't displayed on the items. The shopkeeper quotes 65 CHF for a Victorinox knife that retails for 30 CHF at Coop or Migros, and 25 CHF for a box of Lindt chocolate available for 9 CHF at the supermarket. As travelers on traveler reports and Swiss locals on Threads have observed, Interlaken's Hoheweg strip has some of the highest souvenir markups in Switzerland, with shops targeting day-trippers and tour groups who don't know local retail prices.
scams.avoidance: Buy Swiss chocolate and knives at Coop or Migros supermarkets for standard Swiss retail prices. Check Victorinox.com for official retail prices so you recognize markups. Walk five minutes from Hoheweg to find shops with honest pricing for locals and tourists alike. The Coop and Migros stores near Interlaken West station carry all the popular Swiss souvenirs. Compare prices on your phone before purchasing anything from tourist-facing shops.
scams.location: Souvenir shops along Hoheweg and near Interlaken Ost station

scams.name: The Jungfrau Region Ticket Confusion
scams.tldr: You arrive at Interlaken Ost planning to ride up to Jungfraujoch, the 'Top of Europe.' A person outside the station offers to help you navigate the complex ticket system and save money with a 'local discount.' They sell you a ticket for 180 CHF -- which sounds great compared to the listed 247 CHF.
scams.description: You arrive at Interlaken Ost planning to ride up to Jungfraujoch, the 'Top of Europe.' A person outside the station offers to help you navigate the complex ticket system and save money with a 'local discount.' They sell you a ticket for 180 CHF -- which sounds great compared to the listed 247 CHF. But the ticket only covers the train to Kleine Scheidegg, not the final segment to Jungfraujoch itself. You discover this halfway up the mountain when a conductor tells you to pay an additional 120 CHF or get off at the next stop. Swiss travel forums document that unauthorized ticket sellers and confusing third-party booking offices around Interlaken Ost exploit the genuinely complex Jungfrau railway pricing structure.
scams.avoidance: Buy Jungfrau region tickets only at official Jungfrau Railway counters inside Interlaken Ost or on jungfrau.ch. Check if your Swiss Travel Pass or Half Fare Card provides a significant discount before buying. The official Jungfraujoch return fare from Interlaken Ost is around 247 CHF (2024/25) -- anything much lower is suspicious. Book the 'Good Morning Ticket' on the official site for genuine early-bird savings of up to 30 percent. Download the Jungfrau Railways app for real-time pricing and schedule information.
scams.location: Interlaken Ost station ticket counters and third-party booking offices

scams.name: The Rental Car Speed Trap Fine
scams.tldr: The scenic roads are beautiful, and speed limits seem to change frequently between 30, 50, and 80 km/h zones with small signs that are easy to miss.
scams.description: The scenic roads are beautiful, and speed limits seem to change frequently between 30, 50, and 80 km/h zones with small signs that are easy to miss. Three weeks after returning home, your credit card is charged 250 CHF by the rental company for a speeding fine, plus a 50 CHF 'administrative fee' they tack on for processing. As TripAdvisor's Interlaken forum and traveler reports warn, Swiss speed cameras are among the most aggressive in Europe, and rental companies profit from the processing fees they charge on top of the actual fines. Exceeding the limit by even 1 km/h triggers a ticket.
scams.avoidance: Use cruise control and GPS navigation that displays speed limits on the route. Pay special attention to 30 km/h zones in villages -- cameras are almost always placed there. Consider using trains and the PostBus network instead of renting a car in the Jungfrau region. If you must drive, note that Swiss speed tolerances are near-zero -- stay 5 km/h under the limit. Check your rental agreement for fine processing fees and dispute any unreasonable admin charges.
scams.location: Highways and village roads between Interlaken and Grindelwald or Lauterbrunnen
